title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Bank 1 Sensor 2
plain: The engine computer has found a problem in the circuit for the exhaust gas temperature sensor (bank 1, sensor 2), which measures exhaust heat to protect the turbo, catalytic converter or particulate filter. It usually points to wiring, a connector or the sensor itself.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Particulate filter cleaning may be blocked on diesels
Possible reduced power on some vehicles
checks: Inspect the EGT sensor connector and wiring for damage or corrosion
Check the sensor power, ground and signal with a meter
fix: Repair any damaged wiring or connector first; if the circuit tests good, replace the exhaust gas temperature sensor.

title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Low Bank 1 Sensor 2
plain: The signal from the exhaust gas temperature sensor (bank 1, sensor 2) is lower than the computer expects. This sensor measures exhaust heat to protect the turbo, catalytic converter or particulate filter. A wire shorted to ground or a failed sensor is the usual reason.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Particulate filter cleaning may be blocked on diesels
Possible reduced power on some vehicles

causes.name: Signal or reference wire shorted to ground

checks: Inspect the EGT sensor wiring for rubbed-through or pinched spots
Unplug the sensor and see if the reading changes, which helps separate wiring from sensor
fix: Repair any damaged wiring or connector first; if the circuit tests good, replace the exhaust gas temperature sensor.

title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit High Bank 1 Sensor 2
plain: The signal from the exhaust gas temperature sensor (bank 1, sensor 2) is higher than the computer expects. This sensor measures exhaust heat to protect the turbo, catalytic converter or particulate filter. An open (broken) wire, a bad ground or a failed sensor is the usual reason.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Particulate filter cleaning may be blocked on diesels
Possible reduced power on some vehicles

causes.name: Open or broken signal or ground wire
Wire shorted to a power source

checks: Make sure the EGT sensor connector is fully plugged in and clean
Check the sensor ground and signal wire for an open circuit
fix: Repair any damaged wiring or connector first; if the circuit tests good, replace the exhaust gas temperature sensor.

title: Reductant Injection Air Pressure Sensor Circuit
plain: The engine computer has found a problem in the circuit for the reductant injection air pressure sensor, which monitors the air used to help spray diesel exhaust fluid (DEF) into the exhaust. It usually points to wiring, a connector or the sensor itself.
symptoms: Check engine light on
DEF or emissions warning on the dash
A countdown to reduced speed may start if not repaired
checks: Inspect the air pressure sensor connector and wiring for damage or corrosion
Check the sensor power, ground and signal with a meter
fix: Repair any damaged wiring or connector first; if the circuit tests good, replace the reductant air pressure sensor.

title: Reductant Injection Air Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The reductant injection air pressure sensor is giving readings that don't make sense compared with what the computer expects. This sensor monitors the air used to help spray diesel exhaust fluid (DEF) into the exhaust. The sensor may be failing or the system it watches may have a real problem.
symptoms: Check engine light on
DEF or emissions warning on the dash
A countdown to reduced speed may start if not repaired

causes.name: Failing or out-of-calibration reductant air pressure sensor
Air supply problem in the DEF injection system
High resistance in the wiring or connector

checks: Compare the air pressure sensor reading with related sensors in live data
Check wiring and connector for corrosion or looseness
fix: Confirm the system itself is working, then replace the reductant air pressure sensor if its readings are off.

DEF or emissions warning on the dash

Check the sensor power, ground and signal with a meter
fix: Repair any damaged wiring or connector first; if the circuit tests good, replace the DEF level sensor (usually part of the tank sender).

fix: Repair any damaged wiring or connector first; if the circuit tests good, replace the DEF level sensor (usually part of the tank sender).

title: Reductant Level Too Low
plain: The diesel exhaust fluid (DEF) tank is low or empty. Diesel vehicles need DEF to meet emissions rules, and many will limit speed if it runs out.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Low DEF warning on the dash
Speed limit or no-restart warning if left empty

causes.name: DEF leak from a line or tank
Frozen DEF in very cold weather

checks: Fill the DEF tank with fresh fluid
If the code returns with a full tank, check the level sensor and look for leaks
fix: Refill with DEF; if the warning stays, test the level sensor and fix any leaks.

DEF or emissions warning on the dash

checks: Inspect the DEF injector connector and wiring
Check for power at the connector and measure the part's resistance
fix: Repair any wiring fault first; if the wiring tests good, replace the DEF injector.

checks: Check the DEF injector wiring for rubbed-through insulation
Measure the DEF injector resistance and compare with spec
fix: Repair any wiring fault first; if the wiring tests good, replace the DEF injector.

title: Reductant System Performance Bank 1
plain: The system that sprays diesel exhaust fluid (DEF) into the exhaust isn't working as expected. DEF may not be getting delivered at the right pressure or amount.
symptoms: Check engine light on
DEF or emissions warning on the dash
A countdown to reduced speed may start if not repaired

causes.name: Weak DEF pump or clogged pump filter

checks: Check DEF quality with a refractometer
Run a DEF dosing (quantity) test with a scan tool
Inspect the injector and lines for crystal buildup
fix: Clean or replace the DEF injector or pump as testing shows, and replace bad DEF.

cost.job: Replace DEF injector or pump module
